1.d4 d5 2.c4 c6 3.Nf3 Nf6 4.Qc2 e6 5.Nbd.strategy: Adds a second guard to c4 and supports a later e4: if Black takes on c4, the knight retakes and the queen is not chased by ...b5. The cost is that the knight blocks the c1-bishop, which suits a quiet set-up with a kingside fianchetto better than a quick central break.

Develops the bishop and prepares castling, waiting to see how White commits. It is a modest, solid move: Black keeps the pawn centre and all options of releasing the c8-bishop later. The price is passivity, as White gets the chance to build up slowly.
